q: You load 100 users, then in a loop you `await` one query per user for their orders. How many queries run?
options: 101: one for the list and one for each user
why: A loop with await inside looks innocent, but it sends one trip per item. Count the trips, not the speed of one query.

q: What is the usual fix for N+1?
options: Make the loop run in parallel
Two queries: one for the list, one for all the children with `WHERE user_id IN (...)`, then group in code
Add an index on every column
Cache the first result in a global variable
why: Give empty lists to parents with no children.

q: In GraphQL with DataLoader, why create the loader once per request and not once for the whole server?
options: DataLoader can only be used once
A shared loader keeps a cache across users and can show one user's data to another
why: A per-request loader batches within one request and then is thrown away.

q: A page got slower, but nobody changed the code. What is a likely cause of N+1?
options: The data grew, so the loop now runs many more times. Look at the query log
why: N+1 hides because it is fast with 5 rows and slow with 5000.

q: To fix N+1 you write one giant JOIN of users, orders and payments, and your sums come out too big. Why?
options: Two child lists in one join multiply each other, so each row is counted several times
Payments must be fetched before orders
The index is missing on users
why: One giant join with two child lists fans out and gives wrong sums. Use separate queries, then group in code.
